Sample_characteristics_ch1: cell type: Schwann Cell from Sciatic nerve
Sample_data_processing: Illumina Casava software used for basecalling.
Sequenced reads were trimmed for adaptor sequence, and masked for low-complexity or low-quality sequence, then mapped to Rnor 6.0 whole genome using STAR(v1.26)
Aligned reads were quantified with RSEM
Genome_build: Rnor 6.0
Supplementary_files_format_and_content: tab-delimited files with counts and TPM and FPKM values
Sample_extract_protocol_ch1: A minimum of 10 sciatic nerves was used for the generation of each sample of purified cells. Schwann cells were acutely purified using immunopanning from the injured or uninjured Rat sciatic nerve according to (Lutz, 2014). For injured nerves, only the nerve segment distal to the site of crush injury was included. For uninjured nerves the anatomically equivalent nerve segment was isolated.

RNA from whole nerves was purified according to the RNeasy Fibrous Tissue kit. For injured nerves, only the nerve segment distal to the site of crush injury was included. For uninjured nerves the anatomically equivalent nerve segment was isolated.
Total RNA that passed QC standards proceeded to library synthesis using the Ovation® RNA-seq system V2 (Nugen 7102).

Series_overall_design: RNA profiling of rat Schwann cells after sciatic nerve crush from uncrushed/naïve, 3 days, 5 days, and 7 days post nerve crush
Series_summary: The important contribution of glia to mechanisms of injury and repair of the nervous system is increasingly recognized.  In stark contrast to the central nervous system (CNS), the peripheral nervous system (PNS) has a remarkable capacity for regeneration after injury. Schwann cells are recognized as key contributors to PNS regeneration but the molecular underpinnings of the Schwann cell response to injury remain incompletely understood.

To gain insight into the acute SC injury response, we provide an RNAseq database of Schwann cells purified acutely from the naïve and injured rodent sciatic nerve at 3, 5, and 7 days post injury. Bioinformatic analysis provides validation of cell purity and dataset integrity as well as identification of discrete modules of genes that follow distinct patterns of regulation in the first days after injury and their corresponding molecular pathways.

Our dataset provides a helpful resource for further deciphering the SC injury response and provides a depth of transcriptional data that can complement the findings of recent single cell sequencing approaches. In addition, as more data becomes available on the response of CNS glia to injury, we anticipate that this dataset will provide a valuable platform for understanding key differences in the PNS and CNS glial responses to injury and for designing approaches to ameliorate CNS regeneration.
Series_title: An RNA-sequencing transcriptome of the rodent Schwann cell response to peripheral nerve injury
Series_type: Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
